name_en: Yamanashi's miso-simmered flat noodles, tied to a warlord's legend
summary_ja: 中国の麺料理「餺飩（はくたく）」が奈良・平安期に伝わったとする説が有力で、その音が転じて「ほうとう」になったとされる。戦国期には武田信玄が陣中食として重用し「武田汁」とも呼ばれたと伝わるが、発生地や時期を断定できる定説はない。生麺と季節の野菜を味噌仕立てで煮込む。
summary_en: The leading theory traces the dish to 'hakutaku,' a Chinese noodle dish said to have reached Japan in the Nara or Heian period, its name later shifting to 'hoto.' Legend holds that the warlord Takeda Shingen favored it as army-camp food, giving it the nickname 'Takeda soup,' though no single account of its origin or exact era is settled. Raw noodles and seasonal vegetables are simmered together in a miso broth.
source_publisher: 麺造り百余年 伝承の味 平井屋

name_en: Morioka's miso noodle, adapted from a dish first tasted in Manchuria
summary_ja: 中国東北部の炸醤麺を参考に、屋台から始めた「白龍」の高階貫勝が作り上げたのが始まりとされる。茹でた麺に肉味噌・きゅうり・生姜・ねぎをのせ、混ぜて食べる。食べ終わりに卵を割り入れて出汁を注ぐ「ちーたんたん」も土地の食べ方として定着している。
summary_en: The dish is credited to Takashina Kanshō, who started out selling from a street stall and drew on the fried-sauce noodles he had encountered in Manchuria to develop what became Hakuryu's signature bowl. Hot noodles are topped with stir-fried meat miso, cucumber, ginger, and scallion and mixed together; finishing the meal by cracking an egg into the bowl and adding broth, called 'chi-tan-tan,' is an established local custom.
source_publisher: モリオカ三大麺推進協議会

name_en: Green tea noodles seared on a heated roof tile, from a Yamaguchi hot spring
summary_ja: 明治10年（1877年）の西南戦争で薩軍の兵士が瓦で野草や肉を焼いて食べたという言い伝えを、川棚温泉の旅館経営者が昭和37年（1962年）頃にヒントとして料理化した。熱した瓦の上に茶そば・牛肉・錦糸卵を彩りよく盛り付け、薬味と特製だれで食べる。
summary_en: A local tale that Satsuma soldiers grilled wild greens and meat on roof tiles during the 1877 Satsuma Rebellion inspired an innkeeper at Kawatana hot spring to turn the idea into a dish around 1962. Green tea noodles, beef, and shredded egg are arranged on a heated roof tile and eaten with condiments and a dipping sauce.
source_title: 瓦そば発祥の地 川棚温泉

name_en: Gunma's home-style noodle stew, cooked raw straight into the broth
summary_ja: 養蚕と小麦の里として知られる群馬で育った粉もの料理。幅広の生麺を茹でずにそのまま汁に入れて野菜と一緒に煮込むため、溶け出した打ち粉が汁にとろみをつける。農林水産省の「農山漁村の郷土料理百選」にも選ばれている。
summary_en: The dish grew out of Gunma's tradition of silk farming and wheat-flour cooking. Wide, flat noodles go straight into the pot without pre-boiling, simmered together with vegetables, and the flour that washes off them thickens the broth as it cooks. It is one of the dishes named to the agriculture ministry's list of 100 notable regional foods.
source_publisher: 群馬県製麺工業協同組合
